Ulp. tit. 10. §. pen. ideoque si filius meo tempore quaedam acquisivit ea pater reversus, tanquam sibi iaefita occupare poterit jure peculii: etiam defuncto primum io. l. pen. de suis & legit. & si filio capto, interim pater deinctus fit, ubi reversus fuit suus hæres patri erit. l. 9. C. de postm. revers. alia effecta v. in l. I. §. ult. de SC. Mac. l. 6. §. ult. tutel. l. 13. l. 22. §. I. ff. de capt. & postlim. Est enim Fictio iris commentum ad conciliandam æquitatem cum ratione & ibtilitate juris: Ei versatur quandoque. 1. In Actibus imaginarii. 2. In Personis. 3. circa res. 4. in tempore & loco. v. Tulden. tit.c.6.] Postlimiuium, ut Justiniano Scevolam sequuto placet, dictum est a limine & post: quia ex hostium potestate evadens, redit ad limen, quod amiserat, id est, ad finem, seu terminum Romanae ditionis. d. §. h. n. 3. Servius autem Sulpitius nihil putavit esse in hoc vocabulo notandum praeter particulam post: nam illud limivium, esse tantum productionem vocabuli, t timus in finitimus, referente Cic. in Topic.
main_text.head: Sextus modus Emancipatio.
main_text.p: Quis sextus modus?§ 6. page.notes: Letters a–d in the right margin are reference marks; the superscript marks in the text were read as c and d, and the mark for a is not clearly visible at its place. The printed "83" at top right is read as page 83. The word "impubes" is split as "im-" / "pubes" and completed by the catchword. The black-letter-like italic in "iaefita" (likely "ipsa fictio" or similar) and "postlim." are doubtful. The line "tempore, potestate" and "tit.c.6." are doubtful as printed.
